In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the two graph problems studied, the BSP is superior to the CGM.
the algorithmic complexity of the graph isomorphism problem is between $O(n^{2.5} \log n)$ and $O(2^{O(\sqrt{log n})})$ and the problem is unlikely to be NP-complete.

, in the case of the bipartite graph problem, a CGM with a large number of processors and a BSP with a large number number of processors, and a large amount of memory per processor, will be the most efficient architecture to solve the problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parallel algorithms for the CGM and the BSP have the same time complexity, but different memory requirements.
the algorithms we have presented in this work have a running time of O(n) for the CGM and O(nlogn) for the BSP, where n is the number of nodes in the input graph.

we present the following results: (1) a parallel algorithm for detecting bipartiteness in CGM with O(n logn) steps, (2) a parallel algorithm in BSP with O(n) steps, (3) a parallel algorithm to detect bipartiteness of a graph with O(logn) steps in CGM, and (4) a parallel algorithm with O(logn/loglogn) steps in BSP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CGM model of computation is more powerful than the BSP model for solving these graph problems.
, in the context of the CGM, we can use the same parallel algorithms that have been developed for the PRAM to solve these problems.
the BSP model can be a useful tool for developing coarse grained parallel algorithms for graph problems.
